clue.text: Stringed instrument one moves to the middle — there you are!

indicators.note: something that moves to the middle leaves its old place and is set down in the centre of the word

parts.note: a viola is a stringed instrument a little larger than a violin
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A musician shifts a stringed instrument into the centre and announces it with a flourish.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the I out of VIOLA, leaving VOLA, then put it back in the middle: VO-I-LA.
explanation.definitionFit: Voila is a borrowed French exclamation used when presenting something finished, much like saying here it is.

clue.text: Change in aviator's flying

indicators.note: letters that are flying are tossed about in the air and land in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A pilot notices that something has shifted while up in the air.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's reads as 'is', so the aviator is flying; the letters of 'in aviator' are what fly.
explanation.definitionFit: A variation is an alteration or departure from the usual form, so it is a noun synonym.

clue.text: Picture that is capturing adult in car

indicators.note: capturing means holding something prisoner inside, so one piece wraps around another

parts.note: i.e. is the abbreviation of Latin id est, that is

indicators.note: in places one piece inside another, here the adult going inside the car

parts.note: MG is a British make of sports car
A is the film-certificate abbreviation for adult

explanation.surface: A snapshot catches a grown-up sitting in a car.
explanation.walkthrough: A goes inside MG to make MAG, and that sits between the I and E: I-MAG-E.
explanation.definitionFit: An image is a visual representation such as a photograph or painting, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Draw cart regularly on piece of land

indicators.note: regularly picks letters at even intervals, here every second letter of the word

parts.note: the second and fourth letters of cart
a tract is an area of land

explanation.surface: A horse pulls a cart steadily across a field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Draw' and 'cart' suggest pulling a vehicle, but draw here means to lure; in a down clue 'on' puts the first piece above the second.
explanation.definitionFit: To draw people is to pull them in or entice them, which is the verb's meaning of attract.

clue.text: Noel Edmonds finally wearing new shirt and mac

indicators.note: something wearing clothes is inside them, so this letter goes within the rearranged ones
new means made fresh, so the following letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters of shirt and mac; 'and' just joins them

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the word before it

parts.note: the last letter of Edmonds

explanation.surface: Noel Edmonds, a long-serving British TV presenter, shows up in a new shirt and raincoat.
explanation.walkthrough: Noel looks like a first name joined to Edmonds, but it stands alone as the definition. A mac is a raincoat.
explanation.definitionFit: Noel is an old word for the festive season of carols, borrowed from French, so it names the holiday.

clue.text: Conservative garment for the legs knight picked

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for Conservative
hose are stockings or tights
N is the chess notation for a knight

explanation.surface: A Tory selects a pair of trousers for a knight.
explanation.definitionFit: Chosen and picked are both past participles meaning selected from among several options.

clue.text: Reticent about what tennis player did?

parts.note: re means about or concerning
a tennis player starts each point by serving the ball

explanation.surface: Someone is quiet and withdrawn about how a tennis match went.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the playful description of the second piece; read as RE-SERVED, it is serving again.
explanation.definitionFit: A reserved person keeps feelings to themselves, which is exactly what reticent describes.

clue.text: Chauffeur possibly inflexible about right type of transport

indicators.note: about means going around, so the first word's letters surround what follows

parts.note: set in one's ways means rigid, inflexible
R is the abbreviation for right
a van is a kind of road vehicle

explanation.surface: A rigid-minded driver is particular about the right kind of vehicle.
explanation.walkthrough: Inflexible here means fixed, as in set in your ways; 'possibly' warns that a chauffeur is only one example.
explanation.definitionFit: A chauffeur is a paid employee who drives for an employer, so is one example of a domestic helper.

clue.text: Doctor can hire my equipment

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so these letters are altered in order

parts.note: the letters of the three words

explanation.surface: A medic says they can rent out their kit.
explanation.walkthrough: Doctor looks like a person speaking, but it is the verb meaning tamper with.
explanation.definitionFit: Machinery is a mass noun for machines and apparatus collectively, much like equipment.

clue.text: Dash inside dusty lean-to

indicators.note: inside tells us the letters lie within the run of words that follows

parts.note: the letters run across the two words

explanation.surface: Someone sprints into a grubby shed.
explanation.walkthrough: Dash looks like a quick run, but it is the noun meaning panache.
explanation.definitionFit: Dash as a noun means flair or panache, a showy elegance that matches this answer's meaning.

clue.text: Responses from Republican leader in evading lawsuits

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for Republican

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

parts.note: the first letter of evading
a legal action is a lawsuit

explanation.surface: People react to a Republican politician who dodges court cases.
explanation.definitionFit: Reactions are what someone says or does in reply to an event, so they are plural replies.

clue.text: Iffy Stallone movie

definitions.meaning: second meaning: the 1976 boxing film starring Sylvester Stallone

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like a verdict on a film's quality; the two parts are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means unstable or uncertain, and is also the title of Stallone's famous boxing picture.

clue.text: State a grievance initially with European standard

parts.note: to aver is to state firmly
taken as written

indicators.note: initially points to the first letter of the word before it

parts.note: the first letter of grievance
E is the abbreviation for European

explanation.surface: A complaint is lodged citing a European norm.
explanation.walkthrough: State looks like a noun, a country, but it is the verb meaning declare.
explanation.definitionFit: Average as a noun means the usual or normal level, which is what standard can mean.

clue.text: Understand each student gets stuck in lift

indicators.note: something stuck in another thing is lodged within it

parts.note: a rise is a lift or increase
ea. is the abbreviation for each
L for learner, a student driver

explanation.surface: Every pupil grasps it when they get trapped in an elevator.
explanation.walkthrough: Lift is the British word for an elevator, which the surface leans on, but here it means an increase. L is the learner plate on a student driver's car.
explanation.definitionFit: To realise something is to grasp or become aware of it, a verb synonym spelt the British way.

clue.text: Trendy name for fuel

parts.note: in means fashionable
to name something as evidence is to cite it

explanation.surface: A fashionable label is chosen for a new kind of petrol.
explanation.walkthrough: Fuel looks like a noun, petrol, but it is the verb meaning stir up.
explanation.definitionFit: To fuel anger or unrest is to stoke and provoke it, so the verb means to stir up.

clue.text: Skilful jockey not disheartened

indicators.note: a word that has lost its heart has had its middle letter or letters removed

parts.note: to jockey for position is to compete for it
not with its middle letter removed

explanation.surface: A rider who is not down in the dumps is good at the job.
explanation.walkthrough: Jockey looks like a noun, a horse rider, but it is the verb meaning vie.
explanation.definitionFit: Competent means able to do a task properly, which is close to being adept or capable.

clue.text: Trouble with the woman's shrubs

parts.note: heat is pressure or trouble, as in the heat is on
the possessive pronoun for a woman

explanation.surface: There's a problem with a lady's bushes in the garden.
explanation.definitionFit: Heather is a low evergreen moorland plant with small purple flowers, an example of a small bush.

clue.text: Unknown person scratching bottom left yard in an odd manner

indicators.note: scratching out the bottom of a down word removes its final letter

parts.note: a stranger is someone you do not know
L is the abbreviation for left
Y is the abbreviation for yard

explanation.surface: An unfamiliar figure scratches their backside and walks off in a peculiar way.
explanation.walkthrough: Scratching bottom paints an itchy stranger, but it means dropping the last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Strangely is the adverb from strange, so it describes doing something peculiarly or unusually.

clue.text: Unopened flower on ideal new plant

parts.note: a bud is a flower before it opens

indicators.note: new means made fresh, so the letters before it are remade in another order

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A closed bloom sits on a perfect fresh specimen in the garden.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' puts the first piece above the second.
explanation.definitionFit: Buddleia is a flowering shrub, often called the butterfly bush, so it is one kind of plant.

clue.text: Many run with mouse about

indicators.note: about means moving here and there, so these letters are scattered into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Lots of people scamper off with a mouse on the loose.
explanation.definitionFit: Numerous means great in number, so it is an adjective synonym for a large quantity of things.

clue.text: Rice dish small and extortionate in South American city

indicators.note: in places these pieces inside the word that follows

parts.note: Rio de Janeiro in Brazil
S is the abbreviation for small
OTT, over the top, means excessive

explanation.surface: A rice meal is pricey in a Brazilian city.
explanation.walkthrough: OTT, short for over the top, is British slang for excessive, which fits extortionate prices.
explanation.definitionFit: Risotto is an Italian dish of rice cooked slowly in stock, so it is a rice-based meal.

clue.text: South African golfer's chicken perhaps putting softly at the start

indicators.note: at the start fixes the order, so the soft sign comes before the bird word

parts.note: p is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly
a hen that lays eggs is a layer

explanation.surface: A golfer's chicken is gently putting on the green.
explanation.walkthrough: Putting looks like golf, but 'putting softly at the start' means placing P first.
explanation.definitionFit: Gary Player is a famous South African golfer who won nine major championships.

clue.text: Large sailing vessel nearly capsized touching rear of the iceberg?

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for large

indicators.note: a boat that has capsized is upside down, so in a down clue the word is read bottom to top
nearly means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a cutter is a small single-masted sailing boat

indicators.note: the rear of a word is its last letter

parts.note: the last letter of the

explanation.surface: A big ship nearly turns over after striking an iceberg, like the Titanic.
explanation.walkthrough: Iceberg is a crisp salad variety; the question mark marks it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Iceberg is a pale, crunchy variety of the salad leaf, so the definition gives a kind of it.

clue.text: Trite remark about parasitic insects biting husband

parts.note: c. is the abbreviation for circa, about

indicators.note: something biting holds another thing between its jaws, so it goes around it

parts.note: lice are small blood-sucking insects
H is the abbreviation for husband

explanation.surface: Someone makes a hackneyed comment about bugs nibbling a husband.
explanation.walkthrough: H goes inside LICE, after C: C-LIC-H-E.
explanation.definitionFit: A cliché is an overused phrase that has lost its force, so it is a stale saying.

clue.text: Statements in court Edward made up

parts.note: pleas are what defendants enter in court
Ed is short for Edward

explanation.surface: Edward invented the things he said in court.
explanation.walkthrough: Made up suggests fabricated, but in British slang being made up means delighted.
explanation.definitionFit: Made up is British informal for thrilled or delighted, matching the adjective's sense of happy.

clue.text: More upmarket hotel is scrubbed? Tricky question

indicators.note: something scrubbed is wiped out, so that letter is removed

parts.note: posh means upmarket, so more upmarket is posher
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A smarter hotel has been cleaned, prompting a puzzling query.
explanation.definitionFit: A poser is a puzzling or difficult problem, so it is a stumper that is hard to answer.

clue.text: Rent fell, creating disappointment

parts.note: to let a property is to rent it out
to fell is to knock down, so down can mean fell as a verb

explanation.surface: The rent dropped, which upset the landlord.
explanation.walkthrough: Rent and fell look like nouns or past tenses; both are verbs: let out, and knock down.
explanation.definitionFit: A letdown is an anticlimax that fails to meet hopes, so it is a noun meaning a disappointment.

clue.text: Talk from ordinary judge

parts.note: O is the abbreviation for ordinary, as in O level
to rate something is to assess or judge it

explanation.surface: An everyday magistrate gives a speech.
explanation.definitionFit: To orate is to deliver a formal speech, so it is a verb for speaking at length.

clue.text: Perfume put in the post for the listeners

indicators.note: for listeners means we go by how the word is heard, not spelt

parts.note: something put in the post has been sent

explanation.surface: Fragrance is mailed off to people who will hear about it.
explanation.definitionFit: A scent is a pleasant smell or fragrance, and the word also names bottled fragrance.

clue.text: Cheer one dancing with grace outside university

indicators.note: outside means the rearranged letters wrap around the next piece
dancing letters move around and finish in a new formation

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
U is the abbreviation for university

explanation.surface: Someone gracefully dances in front of a campus crowd who applaud.
explanation.walkthrough: Cheer looks like a noun, a shout of approval, but it is the verb meaning hearten.
explanation.definitionFit: To cheer someone on is to support and hearten them, which is what this verb means.

clue.text: Logical eastern philosophy

parts.note: rational means based on logic
E is the abbreviation for eastern

explanation.surface: It describes a reasoned school of thought from Asia.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests Eastern philosophy as a phrase, but the definition is the last word alone.
explanation.definitionFit: A rationale is the underlying reasoning or principles behind a course of action, its guiding thinking.

clue.text: Some plucky men eventually repelled foe

indicators.note: something repelled is driven back, so the letters are read backwards
some means only part of the following words is used

parts.note: the letters straddle the ends of plucky and the start of eventually

explanation.surface: A few brave soldiers finally drove off their adversary.
explanation.definitionFit: An enemy is someone hostile or opposed to you, the exact sense of an adversary in battle.
